utterances.text: Would you agree that you also knew Sredoje's father Djordje?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The police station in Visegrad, is it close to the green market?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was Wednesday the market day in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps recall that on market days Sredoje's father Djordje dropped by the station to say hello to his son, and if he did not find him there he would leave a message either with you or another one of your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you can't say it happened only on Wednesdays. He dropped by on other days as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was it the same situation when your father dropped by the police station and left messages for you with Sredoje?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When you met in the street, your father, you, and Sredoje, would you shake hands, say hello, ask after each other's health?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In 1982 and 1983, was Sredoje your next-door neighbour?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. He lived in my street.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did he know your brother Osman?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. You should ask him, because I don't have the right to ask him. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Sredoje often visited you at your home?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, if that means anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did he also call on your brother Osman?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I believe so, since he lived in the neighbourhood. If not at his home, then he dropped by at the shop where my brother worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did your father also go to that house where you were with Sredoje?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And when he would call on you he would have to pass by the house where Sredoje lived?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention, but he should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you ever visit Sredoje's home as a guest playing cards, you and your colleague Mr. Hanic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, while he was building a new house I did call on them a few times in that area, Seganje.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was Sredoje a policeman in town, or was his beat around surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: He worked in town, in the traffic police service. He had many duties. It was nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about certain traditions. I hail from a patriarchal community myself. The women in villages, especially in Koritnik village, your birthplace, were they able to visit bars and taverns without husbands?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, they could have but it was not customary.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But married women and mothers with children did not go around bars and taverns?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Don't ask me things like that. My wife didn't go out alone. She did go out with me. I didn't ask other people what they did. Where would I get the right to ask who is going where?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that VG-13 and VG-18 did not know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: They should know him, and if they come here you have to ask them. Plus the -- the opportunity was there. It was possible for them to know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree that among these persons who met their death at Pionirska Street, your father, late Sahib , knew Sredoje the best?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: How would I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You mentioned today that Milan Lukic had never been a policeman.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not that I know of. I've never heard of him being a policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I put it to the Court that it's the Chamber that should decide whether the witness is going on to irrelevant matters. I'm noticing a pattern here. Mr. Cepic by saying the word thank you, he's cutting the witness off from saying the witness's complete answer. If the witness is giving irrelevant information, again I put it the Chamber should decide that, not Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I must say I hadn't noticed that, but, Mr. Cepic, I'll be on the lookout for that, and don't cut off the witness. The witness is entitled to give his answer in its entirety unless the Chamber stops him. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to speed up procedure but if any issue is raised, there's redirect examination and witness can clarify additionally to the OTP, so I'm just trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem is, I mean as you can see from the transcript, while I do know that "hvala" means thank you, it doesn't appear anywhere on the transcript, so it's happening so quickly that the interpreters are aren't able to translate it and put it on the record. Of course, anything that is on the record that we are aware of we will afford ourselves of our opportunity to redirect if necessary. I would just ask that the witness not be interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And please observe the pause between question and answer. Witness, do you hear that? You both speak the same language so there's tendency to overlap, so observe a pause between question and answer and let us ensure that the interpretation is as accurate as is possible. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kurspahic, unlike Milan Lukic, you will agree with me Mr. Sredoje Lukic was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And according to the information that you share, he was a policeman during the first months of the war.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: He was a policeman throughout, until he went to the forest together with 12 other men in the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, you would agree with me that you had an extremely friendly relationship with Sredoje Lukic since you used to call each other "Amidzic"?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I compared the transcripts in both the B/C/S and English languages and I noticed a mistake and I'd appreciate if you could clarify that for me. Am I right to say that during the liberation, Sredoje had short hair? He didn't have a shaved head, he wasn't bald.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I remember whether it was -- he had rather long hair but with a part that was shaved off. Whether it was in the form of a cross or what, I'm not sure. You can ask him, he's here. But I noticed that. He came out with his hands behind his head. I told him, "Amidzic, don't be afraid, I'm here." He's here alive and well and he can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does "Amidzic" have a special meaning? Witness, I was asking, does "Amidzic" have a special meaning?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: There's no special meaning. It -- this refers to sons of two brothers. This is what we Muslims called "Amidzic". This is your brother's son, for example. If it is your sister's son, it's referred to as "Tetic," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also captured there were Niko Vujicic, Dragicevic, although Dragicevic was a higher ranking one, you did call only Sredoje Lukic because you were on friendly terms with him.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: On that occasion when you went your separate ways did you embrace one another, and did you have tears in your eyes?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No. I never approached him. We were about three to five metres apart when I told him that, but when my men came to take him away, I wasn't on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kurspahic, while you were thinking about this event, about this crime, did you ever have any suspicion that it could really have been done by your colleague and friend Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I didn't think along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no. Please give me a specific answer.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No. Why would I suspect that? I could have suspected it if I think he did it. I wouldn't be able to tell -- to do this to me. Allow me to say this to the Court. Don't interrupt me. I wouldn't be able to do to him what he did to me after I saved his life at my own risk without any commands or order. I did it at my own risk, on my own volition, and I risked my life. I released the 13 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it sound reasonable to you that after such kind of relationship that the two of you had he would do something like that to you? Is that logical?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: To a real man it's not logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, when did you first learn that Sredoje had committed the crime against your family?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Approximately in the first half of June. So approximately seven to eight days later. Don't hold me on that. When VG-03 witness came to Medjedja where I was, she told me about what had happened and that my people were not involved there, but after some thinking and making some conclusions, there -- it was not possible that someone of my people were there, but two days later she told me the whole truth from A to Z, how the whole incident evolved and took placement. We were sitting in my office in Medjedja, and she gave me the full account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what was your first reaction when you heard about Sredoje's involvement in those crimes?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: It was hard to believe, but I did believe, and it actually happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But why did you believe it, considering that you had been on friendly terms with him?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I believed the witness who told me about that, because she had no reason to tell me something that was not true. No person would tell you a story that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Witness, I want to verify something in the transcript. When you were asked by Mr. Cole questions about your brother Osman Kurspahic on page 19 of the transcript, you say that your brother -- when you were asked what did you hear happened to him, you say he was executed. Now, on the list of the victims --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: -- of the fire in Pionirska Street there is a person of the same name. Could it be that there were two Osman Kurspahics, two persons of the same name?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. This Osman Kurspahic is a cousin of mine. He is 80 years old, but my brother was born in 1954. He was detained in the Visegrad police administration where he was questioned and interrogated. After that he was transferred to a military facility in Visegrad called Uzamnica. I later found out that he had been executed by Milan Lukic on the compound on that facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, I now have the opportunity just to ask you a few questions on re-examination on matters that have arisen during the cross-examination of two Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Firstly, when and where was it that you heard for the first time the suggestion that Milan Lukic was a police officer in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I heard that from you, Mr. Prosecutor, two days ago here in the OTP. That was the first time I heard about that in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you told Defence counsel you had set fire to some documents on two occasions, and you mentioned April 1992 and the 31st of March, 1993. So I'm --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: -- going to ask you now what type of documents were they that you set fire to in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Those were personal documents of the police administration who were containing full names of people employed with the police, and there were some criminal reports referring to some criminal offences committed at the time in the territory where I was working and also other police records. I destroyed them all by setting them on fire when the Romanija and the Uzice Corps entered, and that happened in the Medjedja police administration which is situated on the right bank of the Drina viewing from Gorazde to Visegrad. The police station was housed in a private house because our police administration that used to be located in the centre of Medjedja had been shelled by the army before and was targeted by the Serbian mortar from -- and heavy artillery from Koriste [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Kurspahic, you mentioned a name a short time ago. Could you give us now the pseudonym for that person.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: That's Witness VG-013. I had her statement. I had also a statement given by a witness which I noted down who had gone to hospital. That was actually not a proper statement. It was my Official Note which she did not sign and the witness mentioned here under the pseudonym also didn't sign it. That was the Official Note. Witness number 114 was in such a serious condition that she was unable to sit down. She wasn't able to sign the Official Note that I made, and I didn't insist on that. And there was some other documents as well which are not related to this case, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can I just clarify that with you? Were there documents relating both to VG-13 and VG-114 that were amongst those that you set fire to in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. Now, you were asked by Defence counsel about not mentioning VG-114 in your statement to the ICTY on the 12th of May, 2000. I just want to ask you this: Were you asked about VG-114 by the investigator who took that statement? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'll ask you now about the time you spoke to VG-13 shortly after the Pionirska Street fire. Did she -- did she identify to you Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Mitar Vasiljevic at that time shortly after the fire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't answer. Mr. Cepic. No, don't answer yet. Let us hear Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that we already have these answers in direct examination, as far as I remember. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The point being made is that the evidence is redundant, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I won't pursue that any further. It was -- it was referred to again, from memory, during the cross-examination. Yes, thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, when you provided the names of the perpetrators of the Pionirska fire in your statement of the 12th of May, 2000, and in your prior testimony in the other trial, who was the person who had told you the names of the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: That was Witness VG-013 and also my father told me directly by giving their full names.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many times did your father tell you the names of the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Look, in a casual conversation you know how it is in families when someone comes who hasn't seen him for a long time, you start these debates within a family circle. Five or six times. Please don't ask me that. This is irrelevant. I'm here in front of you to tell you everything. Please do not tire me with some minor questions that are not relevant for these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I have to tell you that whether a question is relevant or not is a matter for the Chamber to determine. Mr. Cole, you might think now that you have exhausted your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I have a few more matters, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A few matters. Okay. Let's move quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The document that has now been produced by the Defence bearing the number -- in fact, it's now Exhibit 1D25, the list of 15 names of, we'll say police officers, you referred to the stamp on that document. I wonder if that could be shown to you again, Exhibit 1D25. Can you see that document in front of you, Mr. Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, did you say in answer to counsel's question that the stamp on that document was not in use by the police in June in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. It wasn't in use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mischaracter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would object at this time to mischaracterisation of the evidence. I believe he left April of 1992, and he wouldn't have had personal knowledge as to a stamp in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The stamp in the document, was that stamp in use at the time that you last saw a police document in 1992, and was it April?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No. You can establish precisely when the stamp of the Republika Srpska or the Visegrad municipality was designed. One can establish that quite precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just wonder if you can assist us personally. Was the stamp on that document in use in April 1992 when you last saw active police documents?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What type of stamp was in use on police documents, let's say in April 1992, and how would that type of stamp differ from the one in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: As far as the stamp is concerned, it maintained the same round shape. However, we had two in our police administration. The larger one was smaller than this one, and the smaller one was used to cancel some documents inside the police administration, whereas the larger one was put on all official documents that the police issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic asked you about the good relationship that you had with Sredoje Lukic as a police colleague. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So accordingly, you would have had -- you would have no motive to tell lies about Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't even think about it, people. He knows I'm not lying. He's here with us. Please, if there's anything to be clarified in front of this highly esteemed Court, let us clarify the details. I volunteered to be an unprotected witness so that I can be face-to-face with him. I have a moral obligation to say the truth and nothing but the truth. He knows very well that I didn't add even a single comma.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, you were asked by counsel whether you would agree with him that VG-13 and VG-18 did not know Sredoje Lukic. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I never heard anything of the sort. They should have known him. I don't know about that. If they ever appear here, you will have to ask them. There were opportunities for them because Sredoje Lukic was a publicly known figure who was everywhere around the municipality. I don't know about Milan, whether he was in Serbia or not. I don't know whether they knew him, but there were some victims that went to school with Milan Lukic in Prelovo near Visegrad. That is an elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that Sredoje Lukic would also go out for patrols in the villages outside the town of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, on many, many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And how far afield? How far from Visegrad would these villages be at the extreme?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: There's one village further on named Zemljice and Rujiste. Rujiste is the place where Sredoje Lukic was born, and it's about 30 kilometres due north towards Bratunac municipality. That is the furthest village.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Just a couple more questions for you. The capture and release of Sredoje Lukic in April of 1992, can I just ask you if you noticed any signs of injuries or ill-treatment on Sredoje Lukic at that time?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I didn't. It was for a very short time. It didn't last more than a minute. I didn't have anyone's approval to do that. I did it on my own. I stayed there for a short while. I told him that he shouldn't be afraid. I said, "Amidzic, don't be afraid. As soon as night falls I'll come over and release you and transfer you," and that is -- "to Visegrad," and that is how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the last matter I wish to raise with you, Mr. Kurspahic, is when you were talking with VG-13 when she came to Medjedja, from your answers in cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that this question is not raised from the cross-examination. We already discussed what VG-13 said to the witness, and that was in direct examination and again in redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tell us how it arises, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. At page 55 of the transcript the note that I made, the witness was answering questions to the effect that she -- VG-13 told certain facts to the witness but then, I think two days later told the truth about it. I just want to clarify with the witness what the original details were that she told him and what the truth was that she told him some two days later. That's perfectly legitimate, in my submission, and arises directly from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, in answers to counsel you told the Court that VG-13 told you some details about what had happened in relation to your family and then two days later told you the truth about it. My question is this: What was it that she told you on the first occasion, and what was the truth that she told you two days later? If you could just explain that slowly to us, please.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: My first encounter with this person, VG-013, took place in Medjedja sometime in the afternoon. I can't recall the exact date. I've already said it must have been seven or eight days after the entrance of the Uzice Corps into Visegrad. She was wounded. She had the left upper arm bandaged. I asked this person under this pseudonym what had happened and this witness told me that the entire population of that village, the women, children, the elderly, from my were brought to Visegrad and then to Pionirska Street and that on that critical night they were set fire to by Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic and some other men, and my family allegedly did not enter that house. They went to Orlovo instead. And sometime later that night, as I was thinking it all over, I realized it was impossible. That story couldn't have been true. Why would they alone be set free, and then the next day she told me the whole story of that event. I can tell you what she told me, but I wrote it all down in a statement that she wasn't able to sign because I didn't write it in her presence, and I burnt that paper on the 31st of May, 1993, when I left the free territory of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So on the first occasion, VG-13 told you that your family had escaped the fire. On the second occasion, she gave you the awful news that in fact they had perished in the fire.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not a woman --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. We must bring this to an end now, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, sir. Then just one final matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did VG-13 explain why she hadn't told you the truth on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: She told me that she was afraid I would have a heart attack or something and there were no doctors or anything. And then she finally told me the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cole. Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I just ask you for one thing, that Mr. Milan Lukic and Sredoje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, we have procedures that we follow --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm begging you. Please allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have procedures that we follow and we have listened attentively to your evidence, and you have played your part in the procedure. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm begging you, sir. Let me just say if they know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, it's not part of our procedure to have statements from witnesses at this stage. Please leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next Witness is VG-38, and Mr. Ossogo will be leading that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecution is now calling the next witness, VG-038.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm told the witness is slightly inconvenienced but will be here very shortly, so we'll wait. Well, it's been suggested that we take the break now, and I think that's a good idea. Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration. Mr. Cepic. Before the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Your Honour, this morning we received information report from OTP, and this is actually confidential material. Could we go to the private session, please, just for one minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness VG-38.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you feel well enough to answer my questions?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this witness was granted protective measures following an order by the Trial Chamber on the 24th of July, 2001. This is the reason why I shall ask the usher to give him a pseudonym sheet, which is the pseudonym that will be used throughout his testimony. It had been given by way of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness, please look carefully at this sheet and tell me whether you can see your name written on it. Do not say your name, please. Can you see your name on this first sheet you have?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Is it also your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Next I shall ask you to look at the second sheet. There are two -- there's another sheet after the first one. Some names can be found with pseudonyms. If at any time throughout your testimony you want to refer to one of the names during the examination-in-chief or cross-examination by the Defence, please only use the pseudonyms you can see there. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, after the witness has signed the pseudonym sheet we would like to ask for this to be tendered into evidence. Please sign, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted as P43 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-38, do you remember testifying in the Prosecution versus Mitar Vasiljevic case on the 1st and 2nd of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You arrived in The Hague this weekend. Have you had an opportunity to listen to your testimony again in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection is the testimony you have listened to fair to what you said here before this Tribunal before?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecution would like this document to be tendered into evidence. This is the transcript bearing exhibit -- 65 ter exhibit numbers 110 and 111. These were -- this was evidence tendered in the Vasiljevic case through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 110 will become Exhibit P44 under seal, and 111 will become Exhibit P45 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution also seeks to tender documents accompanying the statement made by Witness VG-038 on the 1st and 2nd of October, 2001. They are 65 ter numbers 104, 105, 106, 107, 108, and 109. Document 104 is an aerial photograph showing the town of Visegrad. In the Vasiljevic trial, it had the exhibit number P17.1. Document 105 is an aerial photograph, a black and white photograph, showing the town of Visegrad as marked by the witness. In the Vasiljevic trial it had Exhibit number P17.1.VG-38. As to document 36, it is a coloured photograph of the Pionirska Street showing the school next to the street and the creek that is opposite the school. It was identified and marked by the witness under Exhibit number P17.114.VG-38. As to document 107, it is a photograph showing Pionirska Street and marked by the witness. It's a black and white photograph. In the Vasiljevic case it had Exhibit number P17.3.VG-38. Document 108 is a black and white photograph of the house belonging to Mr. Adem Omeragic that -- in which was the fire, and the photo was marked by the witness showing this house and another two houses in which the Koritnik group had been put up. This was document P17.7.VG-38 in the Vasiljevic case. Finally document 109 shows a series of photographs signed -- there is a signature in the photograph of Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic. It was P17.20.VG-38 in the Vasiljevic case. These were the documents attached to the testimony of Witness VG-038 in the Vasiljevic case which we would like to introduce into evidence further to Rule 92 ter following today's decision by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents will become Exhibits P46, P47, P48, P49, P50 and P51 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to make a suggestion to the Trial Chamber with regard to some of these documents, the black and white photographs. The quality is not very good. Back then we did not have any sophisticated electronic means such as the ones we have today at our disposal. These are documents -- I'm thinking of document 107 in particular. It shows Pionirska Street and was marked by the witness. It was a black and white photograph. Just for the sake of clarity for the Trial Chamber to have a better view of this black and white photograph, we would like to offer a colour photograph that will be given to the registry so that the Trial Chamber can compare both photos and have a better idea of the location of the building. We also have document 108. It, too, is a photograph showing Mr. Adem Omeragic's house as marked by the witness where there was the fire. There, too, we would like to offer an unmarked photo, a colour photo, so that the Trial Chamber can better see the photograph. These are our two suggestions we would like to make to the Trial Chamber for practical purposes, and the Prosecution could have them uploaded electronically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we now in open session or in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, we were in open session when you made your inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: To go from Koritnik to Visegrad, which is the closest village after Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Greben village.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of Milorad Lipovak in that village -- or Lipovac?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What was his trade? What did he do in that village?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I think he was working in Varda company.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was Milorad Lipovac involved in this group of being escorted from Koritnik, the group you were in that was escorted in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. He took us to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What did he tell you as he was escorting you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, that we had to leave the village, that we were no longer safe there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Red Cross, as you said, was he the one that led you to the Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No. It was Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: He used to work as a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Where did he work as a waiter?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: In Panos and in Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you tell us when Mr. Vasiljevic took over from Milorad Lipovac where he led you, where he led you to?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: To Pionirska Street, to the house of Jusuf Memic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were you taken to one or several houses?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: We were in Jusuf Memic's house, and we were in Mujo Memic's house, which is the house across the road from the first one. There were seven of us in Mujo Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You said that there were about seven of you in that house. Can you tell us whether there was any connection, family connection, between Jusuf and Mujo Memic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were father and son.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Who was the father and who was the son?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Jusuf was the father. Mujo was his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You said that there were seven of you in Mujo Memic's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you tell us who you were with in that house?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: VG-13 and the others who had burned. Do you want their names?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Well, if you remember the names you can give us the names.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Hana Kurspahic, Kurspahic Safa, Kurspahic Medo, Kurspahic Medina, Redzo Memisevic, Fazila Memisevic. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: In the second house, Jusuf Memic's house, how many people were there that belonged to the same ethnicity as you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: There were about 60 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: At some point in time did Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic do something in one way or another?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What did they do?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: They asked for money and gold.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When you say "they," you do mean Milan and Sredoje Lukic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you agree to their terms?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. We gave them everything we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: In the evening, at 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And at that time you were in Jusuf Memic and Mujo Memic's house. All the Muslims were in those houses then?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No. When they asked for money and gold, we were -- had all been transferred to Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic obtain the gold and the jewellery from you as you have described, what did they do after that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: They would search us, looking for it… but not Milan, Milan was in front of the house, Milan and Mitar Vasiljevic. Susnjar Milan aka Lalco and Sredoje Lukic were in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I'd like to talk about Milan Susnjar now. He was the third person other than Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic. Were there any other people there?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Milan Lukic; Sredoje Lukic; Mitar Vasiljevic; and Milan Susnjar, aka Laco.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I'd like to spend some time talking about Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic. Let's first talk about Milan Lukic. Did you know him before these events occurred, these events that took place in the Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you discovered that it was him?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: There was some people who went to school with him, so through them I learnt his identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you tell us who these people were, those people that gave you this information? If these people are protected people, please just give us a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: VG-101, and Sajmija Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: These are the two people who told you that it was Milan Lukic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some other people who knew him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know these other people who knew Milan Lukic? Could you give us their names, and if these people are protected, just give us their pseudonym, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are we still in private session? Do we need to be in private session, Mr. Ossogo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we need not remain in private session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question, VG-38. You said that two people who were with you that were of the same ethnicity as you whose names and pseudonym you gave us, outside these two people -- other than these two people, I was just about to ask you did you know these two people who identified Milan Lukic or who told other people in the room that it was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: There was Jasmina Vila, and there was some other people who said that, but I couldn't see them because there was so many of us in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know Jasmina Vila?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Regarding the previous question, "the people who were with you and who came from Koritnik," and not "of the same ethnicity," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know what became of this person after the incident that occurred on the Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: She perished in the fire in the house where we were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I'd like now to move on to the identification of Sredoje Lukic. Did you know Sredoje Lukic before the 14th of June, 1992, which is when the Pionirska Street --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I used to --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: -- and --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: -- see him on the street. He was an official working in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know what position he held in Visegrad, which is where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: He was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you see him in a uniform since you said he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you meet him often?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, on my way to school and back I used to see him in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When you say when you left school, when you went to school, which school do you mean, the one you mentioned earlier, the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you meet Sredoje Lukic before the incident around the Pionirska Street or in your school?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. Don't answer yet. How is that leading, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All references are give to the witness just to say yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-38, you went to the Vuk Karadzic school, didn't you? Could you tell us where you came across Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I was walking across the Rzav bridge, and the police station was nearby. This is where I saw him most often.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How far would this bridge be from the Pionirska area, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: You mean the distance between the Rzav bridge and Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, up to 350 metres, because Pionirska Street stretches up to one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know any people or members of your family who were colleagues of Mr. Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Huso Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just for a short while may we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-38, since you have provided us some information which enabled you to identify Mr. Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic, this information which you provided in addition to your prior statement dated the 2nd of October, 2001, I would now like you to turn your head either to the right or to the left and tell us whether you recognise Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already put forward an objection in principle to this method of identification, and I would like to reiterate that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have in mind the objection you've made, Mr. Cepic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Without it having an impact on your decision, I would like to specify that when these two accused were identified by Witness VG-115 you said, Your Honour, that in light of your discretion you maintained that identifying the accused during a trial like this one is extremely important. In essence, it is very important. You can't exclude one identification method from the other. I think identifying in the courtroom is extremely important. I'm submitting this so that you can weigh all of the material that has been presented to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: VG-38, do you remember the question I put to you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic is on the left. Milan Lukic is on the right -- I mean, the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When you say to the left, could you describe him to us, please, the person and the clothes he's wearing? First describe Milan Lukic to us, please.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Milan Lukic is on the left. Sredoje Lukic is on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you show him to us with your finger, please?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Right and left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And your evidence is that you -- you knew them before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Sredoje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You knew Sredoje before but not Milan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like it to be recorded on the transcript that Witness VG-38 recognised and identified Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object to the identification of Milan Lukic. It would be by exclusion only. I don't think a proper foundation was laid as to the identification of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I may add, during the identification witness said on the left, then on the right, and I was quite confused about that identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It seems to me that ultimately was clarified. Ultimately I think it will be for the Trial Chamber to assess all the evidence and to determine what weight to attach to the witness's identification of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-38, you described in detail what happened in Jusuf Memic's house. Can you confirm that after Mr. Jusuf Memic's house, after you were taken there, where were you taken afterwards?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: They transferred us to the house of Adem Omeragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: When you say you were transferred to Adem Omeragic's house, who took you there?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: The same four men that I named.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you give us their names again, please, for the sake of the record?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, Sredoje Lukic, Milan Lukic, and Milan Susnjar aka Lalco.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What happened in Adem Omeragic's house?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: At around 10.30 in the evening they set us on fire in the house of Adem Omeragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: The entire group of Koritnik you were part of, were all these people in that house?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some other people -- or, rather, women that were brought there from Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Can you describe to us in addition to what you've told us already in your testimony in the Vasiljevic case, what did Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic do, each in turn?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I couldn't see because we were locked up in the house, but I do know that they set us on fire and that there were shots fired at the house where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: VG-38, today you are alive. How can you explain to the Bench in addition to the details you have provided already? Can you tell the Bench how you managed to escape from this house where you were locked up with all the people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: God only knows how I managed to do that. I managed to escape because VG-18 was the first one to break the windowpane and to jump out. Then I jumped out, as well as VG-84. As for the others, I didn't know how they survived. I didn't see, because I didn't dare linger any longer. Both these persons that I named were shooting, shooting at the house in which we were and which was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You told us that you were amongst others VG-013. Do you know what happened to this person?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: I didn't know until the fall of Zepa. I know that she was wounded in that house when I saw her, but I don't know anything relating to what was before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were you in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: No. I was in Zenica. When Zepa fell I moved to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo, we'll take the break now and resume --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just about finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, please finish if you're just about to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: In addition to VG-84 and the other person you mentioned, do you know if other people survived? Can you give us their names and pseudonyms, please?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC
utterances.text: VG-13, VG-018, VG-078, VG-084, VG-101, and Hasib Kurspahic, and Edhem Kurspahic. These are the people who managed to escape from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was the last question I had for this witness, and I would like to refer to the testimony that this witness also gave in the Vasiljevic case. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
